title: hyprfocus.json
description: The hyprfocus declaration: what may exist on the desk, per mode. `base` declares the scene catalog and every other resource; each mode names its active scene SET (with a monitor role per scene) and states the rest as deltas from the base. This is a materialisation model, not a permission model — a scene a mode does not list is not admitted, so there is nothing to ask permission about. A resolver folds base + mode into one complete desk BEFORE anything acts on it, and refuses a mode whose scene set is invalid (unknown scene or monitor role, a scene listed twice, two active scenes claiming the same class). Read by the compositor, the shell and the CLI; written by the shell's mode panel.

version.description: Declaration format version. Bumped when the grammar changes incompatibly, or when the shipped content changes enough that a stored declaration should be re-seeded (LEO-337) — the CLI (`,hyprfocus seed`) reseeds a store whose version is lower than this one, once, without --force.

modes.description: Every mode, keyed by id. `neutral` is the hidden recovery fallback and must exist with `hidden: true`: it is reached from a submap, never listed as a peer of the user-facing modes.

classes.description: Literal class or Lua pattern, matched literal-first so a hyphenated class does not trip on `-` being a quantifier. Also the scene's CLAIM: two scenes active in one mode may not list the same string (compared textually). Two blocks in the SAME scene may share a class only when each also sets a distinct `slot`.

slot.description: Identity suffix (LEO-364) disambiguating same-class blocks within one scene, e.g. `pokemon/chat` and `pokemon/stream` both matching `zen-gaming-media`. With this set, the block only claims a window already carrying the Hyprland tag `slot:<slot>`; `hypr/scene/identify.lua` stamps that tag, once, on whichever live window of the matching class is still unslotted.

order.description:
Position in the left-to-right sequence. With a layout provider this is the order boxes are placed, not a correction applied afterwards.

It is also the block's IDENTITY, not merely a sort key: the compile emits it into the `block:<scene>/<order>` tag every window of the block wears, and a dock's `of` names it (`dofus`'s game block is `order = 0`, so its isles anchor to `block:0`). Zero is therefore a legitimate order — this once required 1 and the shipped declaration silently contradicted it — and renumbering under a running desk orphans that block's live windows.

group.description: All matching windows live in one Hyprland group, so the block is a single tile however many windows it holds.

share.description: Fraction of the work area this block holds.

guard.description: How a non-group block resists being grouped. `deny` also refuses a deliberate toggle, for a tile whose job is to be a fixed region beside a group.

deck_column.description: One column of a `deck`-layout scene (docs/deck.md, `hypr/scene/spec.lua`'s `normalize_columns`). Shows exactly one subscribed thing at a time, flipped through by scrolling.

share.description: Fraction of the row this column holds; columns with no declared share split whatever is left evenly.

classes.description: Literal class or Lua pattern subscribing a window into this column, matched the same way a scene block's `classes` is.

deck.description: Self-declaration name: a window carrying the Hyprland tag `deck:<name>` joins this column regardless of class.

delta.description:
A change to one resource kind. `only` is exclusive and replaces the base's set; `add` and `remove` apply against it. The two forms are mutually exclusive, because a declaration that said both would have no single obvious meaning.

`only` and `remove` differ in how they meet a requirement. `only` says what to inherit, so the requirement closure may still add to it. `remove` is an explicit statement that a resource should not be there, so a requirement that contradicts it is a conflict the resolver reports rather than silently resolving either way — silently starting it ignores what you said, and silently omitting it breaks whatever needed it.

desk.description: A complete desk: every resource that exists, named. This is both the shape of `base` and the shape a resolver produces.

bindings.description:
Binding trees UNDER MODE CONTROL — the ones a mode may withhold. A tree not named here is always available and no mode can remove it.

The default is deliberately 'available', because the two mistakes cost wildly different amounts. A tree missing from this list means a mode does not take away as much as it meant to. A tree wrongly removed means a desk with no terminal and no way back to another mode, which is a reboot. So a mode names what it takes, never what it keeps.

`root` and the modes tree are refused whatever a declaration says: root carries the leader key, and the modes tree is the only way into another mode.

services.description: Background tasks that run, named from the scripts contract's task map rather than as raw units — so the declaration says what work happens and the contract says which units implement it.

projects.description: Projects open on their scene's workspace, named from the projects store.

scenes.description: The scene catalog, keyed by scene name (which is also the workspace name the scene arranges). A scene is active only while the running mode lists it in `scenes`; the catalog itself admits nothing.

drawers.description: The drawer catalog, keyed by drawer id: a small special workspace that slides in over the current scene and holds one app the desk depends on but that never takes a tile (desktop-model.md "Drawers"; today's implementation is docs/shelves.md). A drawer not referenced by any scene's `drawers` list is GLOBAL — reachable from every mode, on the same reserved key it would use inside a scene. One key per drawer everywhere: `key` is validated unique across the whole catalog, so a global drawer's key can never collide with a scene-assigned one either. A drawer absent from the active desk is simply absent from its submap — never shown disabled.

notify.description: Notification routing, keyed by resolved source id (never by the self-reported application name). `default` applies to anything unmatched.

requires.description:
Hard composition edges, keyed by `kind:name`: what a resource CANNOT FUNCTION without. The resolver takes the transitive closure, so a mode that admits `project:obsidian` gets what it needs without listing it. A mode that explicitly `remove`s something required is a conflict the resolver reports.

This expresses composition only. Ordering, readiness and failure handling between the units of one capability belong in the unit files, where systemd already does them better than a resolver could.

Mirrors systemd's `Requires=`. Prefer `wants` unless the resource is genuinely broken without the dependency.

wants.description:
Soft composition edges, keyed by `kind:name`: what a resource USES but can run without. Pulled in by default like `requires`, but a mode may drop it and the resolver honours that silently rather than reporting a conflict.

This is the common case and the one to reach for first. Obsidian without its indexer is degraded, not broken — so a media mode can keep the window and stop the indexing to reclaim resources, which is behaviour that already ships today.

Mirrors systemd's `Wants=`.

dock.description: One isle's dock, or `false` to withhold it on this scene (`hypr/lib/dock.lua`'s `valid_entry`, `hypr/scene/spec.lua`'s `normalize_dock_entry`). A malformed entry is dropped with a report rather than failing the scene, so this schema is the place a typo is caught before the desk silently rests an isle forever.

at.description: The nine-grid cell the isle anchors to, plus the four mirrored corners (`left-top`, `left-bottom`, `right-top`, `right-bottom`) that name the SIDE gutter aligned to one end of it. A corner leads with its dominant axis: `top-left` stands in the top gutter, `left-top` in the left one.

of.description: What the isle hangs off: `screen` (the monitor's own frame), `block:<order>` / `column:<order>` (a block or deck column this scene declares — naming one it does not is reported, since it can never resolve), `slot:<name>`, or `class:<class>`.

orientation.description: Overrides the edge's default orientation for the isle's own layout.

fallback.description: Where the isle goes when this entry cannot resolve — the same grammar, chained.

surface.description: Where one quickshell surface (a popup, a panel — anything not docked to the bar's own frame) is placed inside a scene's published area (hypr repo docs/scenes.md "Areas"). hypr does not read this: it is declaration-only, resolved by quickshell's `services/SurfacePlacement.js` against the hypr-published `geometry.areas` entry for the surface's screen.

of.description: The published area this surface asks for: `work` (the scene's whole usable area), `column:<order>` (a specific block/deck-column box), or `column:first`/`column:last` by declared order.

scale.description: Fraction of the area's width the surface targets, before its own content size and the area's bounds are applied.

valign.description: Vertical placement within the area; defaults to `top`.

drawer.description: A dependency app a scene needs (or the desk always needs) but that must never take a tile: an engine-managed special workspace that slides in over the current scene. Placement, admission and lifecycle are engine policy — this only names what the drawer is and how it starts.

key.description: The reserved key inside the owning scope's submap (mode-level for a global drawer, scene-level for an assigned one). The SAME key everywhere a drawer is reachable — validated unique across the whole `base.drawers` catalog, so it can never collide with another drawer's key in any scope, global or scene-assigned.

class.description: Window class (or Lua pattern) the drawer holds, matched literal-first the same way a scene block's `classes` is.

launch.description: The command that opens the app when no window of its class exists yet. Every launch routes through `uwsm`; the host wraps this command, it does not replace it — so the Ankama launcher's command stays whatever gets it running through Lutris, unchanged from today's `on_created_empty`.

background.description: Launch this drawer silently on mode entry, before any key is pressed, instead of waiting for the first press (desktop-model.md "Drawers"). A background launch failure is logged and never blocks the mode. Declared here; the bring-up executor that reads it ships in a later chunk.

id.description: A stable kebab-case identifier. Names the thing, not the file that happens to implement it, so moving code does not change a declaration.

icon.description: The glyph the bar's mode pill shows next to this mode's name (LEO-425), from the same icon font the bar already uses. Omit and the pill shows the name alone.

hidden.description: Kept out of every user-facing mode listing (CLI `modes`, the shell's pickers, the which-key modes tree). Reachable only as a fallback.

main.description: The scene this mode calls home: where a fresh mode entry lands, and the fallback when a reload cannot restore what a monitor was showing. Must name one of this mode's own `scenes`. Never a periodic correction — focus is not pulled home while the user works elsewhere.

scenes.description: The active scene set, in declaration order. Workspaces are derived from it: a mode admits exactly the workspaces its scenes arrange.

notify.description: Routing overrides merged onto the base's, keyed by source id. `default` sets the fallback for this mode.

revoke.description: Per-resource revocation overrides for this mode, keyed by resource id.

presentation.description:
How the desk looks while this mode runs. Passed through by the resolver untouched; the shell owns its meaning.

`palette` is a LEASE, not a write (LEO-288): while the mode runs the desk shows this palette, and when it ends the baseline (the sun's, or the user's pick) comes back untouched. Omit it and the mode tints nothing — `accent_role` already picks a role within whatever palette is active, and this optional field is for the rare mode that must pick a different palette altogether. Wallpapers belong to palettes, not modes (LEO-365): the theme store's per-palette `wallpapers` binding is what changes the image, so a mode has nothing more to lease for it.

palette.description: The palette leased while this mode holds. Either a plain id (leased at every hour) or a `{ day, night }` pair (LEO-365) leased by the clock — day is 07:00 (inclusive) through 18:59, the same split hypr's `,theme.sh` `daytime()` uses. Must name a variant the shell carries (Theme.qml / a theme pack); an unknown name reads as no lease — resolution never fails.

ref.description: A resource reference, `kind:name` — `scene:`, `binding:`, `service:`, `project:`. Singular, and qualified because requirements cross kinds. A `scene:` reference is CHECKED, never added: a mode that admits something requiring a scene it does not list is refused.

revocation.description: What happens to a resource a mode stops admitting. `hold` parks it out of sight and restores it when the mode ends; `retire` stops it and does not bring it back. Holding buys attention, retiring buys capacity — so windows usually hold and services usually retire.

blocks.description: Ordered groups of window classes sharing the workspace.

barred.description: Classes that legitimately open here without belonging to a block. Barred because auto_group grabs whatever opens while a group holds focus.

bindings.description: Binding trees admitted while this scene is active. A tree is enabled if the mode admits it OR the active scene admits it; scene-admitted trees follow the workspace, not only the mode (LEO-266).

strays.description: What happens to a window matching no block: `slot` gives it a tile, `float` floats it above the declared split so the split never shifts.

gaps_in.description: Scene-declared inner gap (LEO-397), in px: wins over the host workspace-spec and the global `general:gaps_in` where set.

gaps_out.description: Scene-declared outer gap (LEO-397), in px or per side ({top,right,bottom,left}); same precedence as `gaps_in`. Must be a single number or a plain object with only numeric sides.

bar_follows_scene_gaps.description: Deprecated, ignored since LEO cross-repo 'bars never dance': an isle that is not docked now rests at a fixed position that depends on its monitor only, never on the scene or its gaps. Kept in the schema (rather than removed) only so a live store still carrying this field on every scene — written before the retirement — does not fail schema validation; a fresh seed no longer sets it.

icon.description: The glyph the bar's workspace pill shows for this scene's workspace (LEO-343), from the same icon font the bar already uses. Omit and the bar falls back to a numeric/dot glyph, the same as an undeclared workspace.

drawers.description: Drawers assigned to this scene, by reference into `base.drawers`. Reachable on their reserved key only while this scene is active (locking the scene does not withdraw them); a drawer may be assigned to more than one scene without duplicating its declaration. Every id here must exist in `base.drawers` — an unknown reference is a declaration error, checked the same way an unknown scene reference is.

layout.description: Opt-in to the deck layout (docs/deck.md): every scene defaults to `scene` (fixed blocks); `deck` reads `columns` instead and flips one thing per column at a time. `blocks` still governs auto-grouping/barring under either layout — `columns` only decides deck placement.

columns.description: A `deck`-layout scene's columns, 1-3, left to right. Ignored (and normally omitted) under `layout: scene`.

docks.description: Where each of the bar's isles stands while this scene is active (docs/scenes.md "Docks"). Keyed by isle id (`bar.workspaces`, `bar.clock`, `dofus.roster`, …). `false` withholds the isle on this scene entirely; an entry says which target it hangs off and at which anchor. An isle whose target has no live window rests at its bar seat instead — resting is a state, not a failure.

surfaces.description: Where quickshell's own popups/panels are placed inside this scene's published area (docs/scenes.md "Areas"), keyed by surface id (`notifications`, `toasts`, …). hypr does not read this field at all.

scene_placement.description: One active scene of a mode and the monitor role it is placed on.

monitor.description: A host monitor ROLE (conf/hosts/*.lua `primary_monitor`/`secondary_monitor`), never a raw output name. The mode's role wins over the host file's workspace pin; a role whose output is missing falls back to primary, and the scene moves back when it returns.

spawn.description: One companion a block's presence keeps alive: launched when the block has a member and fewer than `max_spawns` of its class are on the desk, closed when the last member leaves. With `auto_start` it also opens whenever the scene is active, even before the member maps. Not a claim — presence is derived from live windows, never remembered. The engine folds the singular block `spawn` into the same shape.

class.description: The companion's identity, matched against live windows.

command.description: What runs the first time in (spawned through uwsm).

max_spawns.description: Cap on how many of `class` the engine keeps alive while the block has a member.

auto_start.description: Keep the companion alive whenever the running mode admits this scene, even with no member window currently present.

spawns.description: Several companions sharing one block's presence, as a list of `spawn` entries — one block naming a console and each of its browsers, say. The singular `spawn` and this list fold into the same normalized `block.spawns` in the engine, so a consumer reads one shape.

verdict.description: What a notification does on screen. History records every notification with the verdict applied to it regardless — suppression governs what interrupts, never what is knowable afterwards.
